Scope: Comprehensive offline Turkish-English research synthesis. Existing 32-sentence translation experiments reused; no new translation benchmark performed during this synthesis. Language-identification tests are a separate 150-example task.
SizeDefinition: Decimal disk bytes, not RAM. Selected files supporting both directions; runtime excluded. ONNX totals below include encoder, merged decoder, fast tokenizer JSON and SentencePiece file. These tokenizer formats are alternative consumption paths, so a deployment can omit the unused one. Small configuration files add negligible space. No all-variant repository totals.

ExistingEvidence.scope: Offline Turkish-English translation in both directions; research and isolated experiments only
ExistingEvidence.recommendation: Toz-Cevir-1 q8 for the smallest tested balance of usable translation quality and package size; Mozilla Bergamot tiny for minimum storage and latency

method.sizeUnits: Decimal MB and GB; model files, not process memory or the complete application
method.inference: Local files only; llama.cpp offline mode with a loopback endpoint, local Bergamot WebAssembly and local ONNX Runtime
method.parameters: Bergamot beam=1 and beam=4, single WebAssembly worker; Toz beam=4 with official sentence splitting, four CPU threads; language models greedy decoding, four CPU threads, 2048-token context, reasoning disabled
method.lmtPrompt: Official source-language/target-language labels and translation instruction from the model card
method.assessment: Direct bilingual review of the actual outputs, not a large public benchmark or a percentage accuracy estimate

candidates.name: Mozilla Bergamot tiny en-tr + tr-en
candidates.status: Tested, both directions, beam=1 and beam=4
candidates.assessment: Smallest tested package and lowest latency. Useful ordinary translations, with awkward grammar and errors in idioms, nested meaning and negation. Beam=4 fixed the unavailable-network polarity error observed with beam=1.

candidates.name: TozAI/Toz-Cevir-1 q8
candidates.assessment: Best tested small candidate on this corpus. Mostly usable ordinary and technical sentences. Failed the Turkish double negation and flea/camel idiom, and partially mistranslated the English call-it-a-day idiom.

candidates.name: Argos Translate English-Turkish 1.5 pair
candidates.assessment: Two directional packages. Existing published Mozilla comparisons place these Argos versions below Bergamot on the reported Turkish-English datasets.

candidates.name: Gemma 3 270M instruction tuned, Q4_K_M
candidates.assessment: Unsuitable in this experiment: six empty outputs, frequent source copying or an acknowledgement instead of translation, poor Turkish output.

candidates.name: Qwen3 0.6B Q4_K_M
candidates.assessment: Frequent omitted content, untranslated input, repetition and incorrect Turkish. Not selected.

candidates.name: Hy-MT2 1.8B 1.25-bit v2
candidates.status: Downloaded and hash verified; local loading failed before any translation
candidates.assessment: Promising specialized translation model with Turkish support. This file requires the specialized sparse ternary implementation; the tested stock llama.cpp b11960 rejected tensor offsets. Translation quality was not graded.

candidates.name: NiuTrans LMT-60 0.6B Q4_K_M
candidates.status: Tested, both directions, official labelled prompt
candidates.assessment: Useful technical and ordinary translations, but many meaning and fluency errors, especially English-to-Turkish. Worse than Toz on this corpus despite the larger package. Generic prompts performed worse; those exploratory outputs are retained separately.

candidates.name: Qwen3.5 0.8B IQ4_XS
candidates.assessment: Frequent meaning errors. For example, English bus became Turkish refrigerator; November became April. Not selected.

candidates.name: OPUS-MT tr-en base + en-tr tc-big, selected quantized ONNX files
candidates.assessment: Ready ONNX packaging is larger than the preferred limit. Other CTranslate2 packaging/quantization can reduce disk size, but no smaller package was produced in this experiment.

candidates.name: QuickMT English-Turkish directional pair
candidates.assessment: Published English-to-Turkish and Turkish-to-English benchmark results are promising. Ready weights are float16; an approximately 400 MB int8 pair is a conversion estimate, not a verified package.

candidates.name: Hy-MT2 1.8B standard Q4_K_M
candidates.assessment: Standard four-bit alternative to the specialized low-bit file, above the preferred size limit.

candidates.name: TranslateGemma 4B Q4_K_M
candidates.assessment: Dedicated translation model in the larger fallback tier, within the hard limit but well above the preferred size.

candidates.name: Google ML Kit on-device translation
candidates.status: Researched; Android option, not tested on a phone
candidates.assessment: English and Turkish are supported. Official mobile API; not a directly supported Windows plugin. The exact Turkish-English installed size was not measured.

AdditionalCandidates.Assessment: Ready community ONNX export with English and Turkish, direct many-to-many translation. Original model is distilled from M2M-100. No local Turkish-English quality score.

AdditionalCandidates.LocalTest: Only the special 1.25-bit file was attempted; it failed to load. No local quality assessment.
AdditionalCandidates.Name: Hy-MT2 1.8B
AdditionalCandidates.Runtime: Model cards require STQ kernels for 1.25-bit and 2-bit variants, PR 22836 and PR 19357 respectively. Standard four-bit variant is offered separately.

AdditionalCandidates.Name: TranslateGemma 4B
AdditionalCandidates.Assessment: Dedicated Google translation model with Turkish support. The GGUF text model is sufficient for text translation; image projection weights are for image input.
604M Turkish chat model, separate from Toz-Cevir-1. Translation quality unmeasured. The model card describes Turkish-focused training and weak other-language capability.

QuickMT.Int8Status: Conversion estimate only; no such package was produced or verified.
QuickMT.ScoreMeaning: COMET22 estimates translation quality; these scores are not percentages of correct sentences. Results are publisher-reported head-to-head evaluations.

Integration.ONNX: Official Microsoft.ML.OnnxRuntime C# package, plus tokenizer and generation code supplied by each model project.
Integration.CTranslate2: Ready native inference library; the examined QuickMT examples use Python. No ready .NET integration was verified during this research.
Integration.GGUF: Native llama.cpp engine; a .NET wrapper such as LLamaSharp can expose it to C#. Model-format support remains specific to the chosen model and runtime.
Integration.MLKit: Official on-device Android/iOS translation; models around 30 MB per language model. Turkish/English supported. Phone pair footprint and local quality not measured; no official Windows target.
Integration.Bergamot: Reuse supplied JavaScript/WebAssembly in existing BlazorWebView with a small separate JavaScript module and C# interop; no separate Node runtime. Agreed implementation approach, not yet integrated.

Clarifications.Tests: 150 examples (58 words and 92 phrases/sentences) were language identification. Translation experiments used a separate 32-sentence corpus, 16 per direction.
Clarifications.UserPriority: The user clarified that small differences in download size are curiosity rather than the main integration criterion.
Clarifications.DetectorMaintainers: No Turkish-English translation model found in the inspected Lingua, TinyLD and franc projects/maintainer profiles. No unfinished translation model was found either.

EvidenceLimits: Published quality comparisons and local output reviews are labeled separately. Unmeasured latency is omitted. Larger general-purpose models were not exhaustively enumerated; dedicated translation families and previously tested small models are the focus.
